description: Baseline of Next-Generation Arctic Marine Shipping Assessments - Oldest Pan-Arctic Satellite Automatic Identification System (AIS) Data Record of Maritime Ship Traffic, ancillary data 2011-2012 is a data set deposited in UC Santa Barbara by its authors Paul Arthur Berkman, Greg Fiske (Science Diplomacy Center, Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, Tufts University). The Arctic is prominent in the history of the International Maritime Organization (IMO), following the RMS Titanic disaster in 1912 and soon signing in London of the Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea in 1914. Eighty years later, the IMO initiated a process to manage shipping in ice-covered oceans. Coverage: not stated; the metadata date the deposit to 2020. The repository holds 2 deposits of this kind (versions, parts or per-site or per-year releases); this record describes the series through its most recent member and lists the others in the notes. Formats: XML. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is not stated (no licence in the DataCite metadata read on 2026-09-29). Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet for this repository.
